summary.text: Plants are the organisms of the kingdom Plantae, and most are photosynthetic, making sugars from sunlight, carbon dioxide and water.
The sugars plants make provide the energy for most of Earth's ecosystems, and animals are herbivores or otherwise dependent on plant materials.
Aristotle's plant kingdom held every living thing that was not an animal, but current definitions exclude fungi and some of the algae.

facts.label: Known species
facts.value: About 380,000, most of them seed producers

facts.label: Size range
facts.value: From single cells to the tallest trees

facts.label: First land plants
facts.value: Around 450 million years ago, in the Ordovician

items.prompt: An old botany book lists fungi among the plants, just as Aristotle's biology did. How do current definitions treat fungi?

options.label: They keep fungi as a type of plant
They place fungi inside the green algae
They leave fungi out of the plants
They treat fungi as the ancestors of land plants

items.explain: Aristotle's plant kingdom held everything that was not an animal, fungi included, but definitions have narrowed and current ones exclude fungi.

items.prompt: A deer eats grass on a hillside. Where did the energy in that food first come from?

options.label: Sugars the grass made from sunlight, carbon dioxide and water
Minerals the grass pulled out of the soil
Heat stored in the ground beneath it
Oxygen the grass gave off into the air

items.explain: Plants use chlorophyll to turn sunlight, carbon dioxide and water into sugars, and animals depend on plant materials for energy.

items.prompt: Over time, some plants stopped relying only on sunlight and began taking energy from other organisms. What is such a plant called?

options.label: Herbivorous
A glaucophyte
An embryophyte
Parasitic

items.explain: Some plants evolved to be parasitic, meaning they take energy from other organisms.

items.prompt: Someone claims every plant is a tall tree you could stand beneath. Which fact shows the range is wider?

options.label: Every plant is at least a metre tall
Plants run from single cells up to the tallest trees
Plants stay small, since the tallest ones are algae
The tallest plants are only a few metres high

items.explain: Plants in a broad sense range in scale from single-celled organisms to the largest trees.

items.prompt: A florist guesses that plants with blossoms are a rare corner of the plant world. What does the species count say?

options.label: A small group: about 10-15% of species
Roughly half of all species
Most of them: about 85-90% of species
Barely any, since most plants are ferns

items.explain: About 85-90% of all plant species are flowering plants.

items.prompt: Before any plant stood on dry ground, where did the ancestors of land plants live?

options.label: They evolved in water
They evolved on bare rock
They evolved in volcanic soil
They evolved in dry caves

items.explain: The ancestors of land plants evolved in water.
